Klassiper.description: The government-appointed land survey official whose arrival and actions drive much of the chapter's conflict; also referred to as the Classiper or Klassiper Kochupillai.

Kodanthara Moothassan.description: A senior community leader and head of the Kodanthara family, involved in temple and village affairs.

Kanakku Pillai.description: The temple administrator responsible for managing temple affairs and implementing orders.

Ponnu Thampuran.description: A local feudal lord or royal figure whose authority is invoked by officials and villagers.

Thampuratti Amma.description: The wife of Ponnu Thampuran, remembered for her regal appearance and status.

Kunjudevi.description: A woman who helps clean the Erumathramadam and recalls seeing Ponnu Thampuran and Thampuratti Amma.

Mani.description: A woman who helps clean the Erumathramadam with Kunjudevi and Kunnukki.

Kunnukki.description: A strong-willed woman who voices opinions on social equality and opposes tradition.

Pottachi.description: Nickname for Kunjukki, known for her outspoken nature.

Kunjilakshi.description: A woman who warns Kunjukki to be careful with her words about the Thampuratti.

Kuruppachan.description: A respected elder and community leader, involved in land and temple matters.

Asan.description: A learned man or teacher, often consulted for advice and involved in temple administration.

Achoman Mama.description: A storyteller and elder whose tales about family histories are well known in the village.

Idramankonthi.description: A past Karanavar (family head) who managed land leases and family affairs.

Kochupillai.description: The Classifier, a land surveyor, described as handsome and married to Kunjulakshmi.

Kunjulakshmi.description: Kochupillai's wife, described as dark-skinned and stout, who desires status and a child.

Subbaiyan Swami.description: The royal cook for the Maharaja, known for his connections and personal stories.

Bhavathi.description: Subbaiyan Swami's second wife, formerly a wet nurse in the palace.

Yandan.description: A handsome clerk at the Kilimanoor palace who marries Bhavathi's daughter.

Devadi Mullakkaran.description: Klassiper's attendant who manages the collection of gifts and bribes for officials.

Erikkillathu Pappu.description: A local man who announces the new standard for offerings to the Classifier.

Pappu Panikkar.description: A family manager who is shocked by the high cost of the new gold coin offerings.

Kunju Lakshmiyammai.description: Klassiper's wife, who desires rare gold coins and status.

Ittirachikkaimal.description: The present head of the Pullattu family, involved in the story of the Nagarasi treasure.

Cheyya Mullakkaran.description: A Mullakkaran who tries to obtain a Nagarasi gold coin for Kunju Lakshmiyammai.

Unnooliyamma.description: The aged sister of the present Mullakkaran, reflecting on her family's decline.

Paacharan.description: Unnooliyamma's younger brother and the current Mullakkaran.

Seerattak Kaimalan.description: A community leader involved in village and temple decisions.

Konnothu Pillai.description: A community leader who helps arrange accommodations for officials.

Sankaran Annaavi.description: A cook brought in to prepare food for the visiting officer.

Balathol Mukundar.description: A prominent Brahmin and chief priest of the temple for fifty years.

Kochumichar.description: A villager known for supplying rice to the royal household and for his palace stories.

Paru.description: Kochumichar's daughter-in-law who listens to family stories.

Thattachari Samimoopar.description: A goldsmith who advises Kunjulakshmi to have a gold child crafted.

Nangaiyar.description: A servant woman in the Kodantra household who raises Kunjammai.

Kochu Pennu Kunjammai.description: The only remaining female descendant in the Kodantra house, raised by Nangaiyar.

Ittikkuruppu.description: The present elder Asan of the Kodantra household, widowed and childless.

Ayyappa Kuruppu.description: Younger brother of Ittikkuruppu and next in line as household head.

Seshaiyyan.description: A young Pattar (Brahmin) from Thiruvananthapuram who marries Kunjammai.

Kochachasan.description: A member of the Kodantra household who receives Seshaiyyan.

Chakki.description: A woman with whom Seshaiyyan has a relationship after his marriage.

Kalyaniyammai.description: A renowned midwife from Seelandhippillai, also skilled in copying manuscripts.

Paramu Vathiyar.description: The head of Seelandhippillai, a learned guru and spiritual leader of the village.

Kochittuli.description: Paramu Vathiyar's wife, originally from Malabar, who was left destitute after a plague.

Nagampillai.description: Tamilian surveyor who leads the group of measurers, rival to Klassiper.

Paruthikkattu Othai.description: A Christian oil supplier who serves Nagampillai and aspires to build a church.

Orodhai.description: Outhai's wife, who works at the oil press.

Varkki.description: Outhai's son, who also works at the oil press.

Mangalacheri Iravippillai.description: Head of the Mangalacheri family, registers new land and manages family affairs.

Kochunnyamma.description: Iravippillai's wife from Vaipparacheri, respected as Periyamma.

Pachaalathu Kodhai.description: A former Periyamma of Mangalacheri, known for her harshness.

Valiyamaani Paatti.description: An elder woman of Mangalacheri who stands up to Periyamma.

Kunjanda Pillai Mama.description: A past head of Mangalacheri, husband of Pachaalathu Kodhai.

Thampi Muraikkaran Madhupillai.description: Next in line to head Mangalacheri, leads a rival family faction.

Kochumaniyammai.description: Madhupillai's wife, who schemes to become Periyamma.

Pappummaavan.description: Iravippillai's elder brother, unfit to be karanavar.

Kochukoathai.description: Pappummaavan's wife from the Chaanakathara family.

Kochukothai Akka.description: Kochukoathai, considered for the role of senior aunt at the wedding.

Kochumani.description: Kochumaniyammai, who tries to elevate Kochukothai Akka's status.

Seelandhippillai Paramu Vathiyar.description: The spiritual leader and guru of the village, head of Seelandhippillai family.

Krishnankovindan.description: Paramu Vathiyar's former manager in Alappuzha and Kochittuliyamma's husband.

Vaaryanthara Kochittuliyamma.description: Krishnankovindan's wife, left alone after the plague.

Kochidvoori.description: A maiden from Kaplangattu Mana in Malabar, ancestor of the Varyanthara family.

Unni Namboothiri.description: A young Namboothiri who elopes with Kochidvoori.

Vezhapra family.description: A family of Pallichanmar (palanquin bearers) ostracized for ritual defilement.

Erumathramadam.description: A guesthouse or lodging near the temple, traditionally reserved for Brahmin priests.

Sthanikars.description: Community leaders or temple administrators with authority over temple affairs.

Sudra.description: A member of the fourth varna (caste) in the traditional Hindu social hierarchy.

Namboothiri.description: A high-caste Brahmin community in Kerala, traditionally temple priests.

Thantris.description: Brahmin priests who perform temple rituals and ceremonies.

Tahsildar.description: A revenue administrative officer in charge of land and tax matters.

Ambalappuzha.description: A town in Kerala, known for its famous Krishna temple.

naivedya prasadam.description: Sacred food offered to the deity and then distributed to devotees.

rajabhogam.description: A share of agricultural produce given as tax to the ruling authority.

taluka.description: An administrative division or sub-district in India.

tandalkaran.description: A land agent or local revenue official responsible for measuring and collecting taxes.

marumakkathayam.description: The matrilineal system of inheritance practiced in parts of Kerala.

marakkals.description: Traditional units of measurement for grain or land in Kerala.

chakrams.description: Old silver coins used as currency in Kerala.

Vettikkattu.description: A paddy field or area of agricultural land in the village.

Hanuman.description: A Hindu deity, symbolizing strength and devotion.

Devasthanam.description: A temple trust or institution that owns and manages temple property.

Mangalaseri family.description: A large, industrious family in the village known for their agricultural work.

Nagarasi.description: A rare and valuable gold coin, highly prized as an offering.

Pullattu family.description: A family in the village with a legendary treasure story.

Idyathikaimal.description: A past head of the Pullattu family, associated with the treasure legend.

karisal.description: Marshy or alluvial land, often newly cultivated.

Marutha.description: A clan deity worshipped by the Pulayar community.

Pulayars.description: A Dalit community in Kerala, traditionally agricultural laborers.

Dharmasastha.description: A Hindu deity, often identified with Lord Ayyappa.

Thiruvananthapuram.description: The capital city of Kerala, seat of royal and administrative power.

Madappalli.description: The temple kitchen or royal kitchen.

Kandavarnan.description: A reference to a handsome, high-caste man, possibly mythological.

Panikkar.description: A title for a martial arts teacher or family manager.

marakkal.description: A traditional unit of measurement for grain or land.

Ezhupura.description: A verandah or open hall in a traditional Kerala house.

kalari.description: A traditional martial arts training hall.

Pattar.description: A Tamil Brahmin, often brought in for religious ceremonies.

thali.description: A sacred necklace tied during Hindu marriage ceremonies.

namaskara rice.description: Rice offered as part of a ritual meal for Brahmins.

angavastram.description: A traditional upper cloth worn by men in South India.

tulasi.description: Holy basil, used in Hindu rituals and as a hair adornment.

naazhigai.description: A traditional unit of time in South India.

mamathu.description: A raised mound or embankment, often near water bodies.

Seeratta family.description: A prominent family in the village with a Brahmin lodging.

Pattars.description: Tamil Brahmins, often brought for rituals.

Ganapathippotri.description: A Brahmin husband of Siruthakunjammai in the Seeratta family.

Siruthakunjammai.description: The eldest woman in the Seeratta family.

Paruthikkattu.description: A house or family associated with oil supply, belonging to the temple.

Konnotthu.description: A family or location in the village.

Chanakathara.description: A family or house in the village.

neyyappam.description: A sweet fried rice cake made with ghee, served at ceremonies.

pandal.description: A ceremonial canopy or temporary structure for weddings.

Mrityunjaya homam.description: A Vedic ritual for longevity and protection from death.

Gita Govinda.description: A classical Sanskrit text, often copied by skilled scribes.

Chithirai.description: A month in the Tamil calendar (April-May).

Padeni.description: A street play or festival performance at the temple.

thullal.description: A satirical dance-drama form from Kerala.

chovan.description: A type of performance or character in temple festivals.

geethangal.description: Songs, often performed during temple festivals.

parayan.description: A reciter or performer of religious texts.

kakkan thullal.description: A specific style of thullal dance.

Kasi.description: The holy city of Varanasi, a major pilgrimage destination.

dakshina.description: A traditional offering or fee given to priests or teachers.

Chandali.description: A term for an outcaste woman, used here as an insult.

Kaplangattu Mana.description: A Nair family in Malabar, Kerala.

Thiruvambadi.description: A place in Alappuzha where the Varyanthara family settled.

Varyanthara.description: A family founded by Kochittuli and Unni Namboothiri.

Alappuzha.description: A city in Kerala, known for its backwaters and trade.

pottu.description: A decorative mark worn on the forehead by women.

toddy.description: An alcoholic beverage made from the fermented sap of palm trees.

backwater.description: A network of interconnected canals, rivers, and lakes in Kerala.

madam.description: A guesthouse or lodging, often attached to a temple.

prasadam.description: Food offered to a deity and then distributed to devotees as a blessing.

chakram.description: An old silver coin formerly used as currency in Kerala.

sambandham.description: A traditional form of relationship or marriage among matrilineal communities.

mundus.description: A traditional white cotton garment worn by men and women in Kerala.

homam.description: A Vedic fire ritual performed for specific purposes.

naivedya.description: Food offered to a deity during worship.

karanavar.description: The head or senior-most male of a matrilineal family.

matrilineal.description: A system of inheritance and lineage traced through the mother's line.

Pulayar.description: A Dalit community in Kerala, traditionally agricultural laborers.

Gandharva.description: A celestial being in Hindu mythology, often associated with music and romance.

Gandharvan.description: A male Gandharva; here, also refers to a mysterious or supernatural lover.

Sthanikar.description: A temple administrator or community leader.

punugu.description: A fragrant substance used in traditional perfumes.

parijata.description: A fragrant night-flowering tree, also known as night-flowering jasmine.

kakkan.description: A character or style in thullal performances.

sari.description: A traditional garment worn by women in India.

bhajan hall.description: A hall or space in the temple designated for devotional singing.

thaali.description: A sacred necklace tied during Hindu marriage ceremonies.

Konnothu Valyachan.description: The patriarchal elder of the Konnothu family, responsible for the administration and keys to the Devasthanam treasury; his death marks a generational shift.

Kodanthra Moothassan.description: The respected elder of the Kodanthra family, known for his righteousness and ability to discern the temple's naivedya prasadam; his death leaves a leadership void.

Seerattakaimal.description: A senior leader from the Seeratta family who inherits the Devasthanam treasury keys after Konnothu Valyachan; later grows old and weary.

Ayyappakuruppu.description: Son-in-law of Kodanthra Moothassan, becomes the Moothassan of Kodanthra; involved in family property disputes and court cases.

Kallaraykkal Raman Pillai.description: A member of the Kallaraykkal branch, next in line for Konnothu Valyachan's position; faces financial struggles and property disputes.

Ganapathi Ayyar.description: A powerful Brahmin landlord and moneylender from Mangombu, who accumulates land and wealth through loans and mortgages.

Swami.description: Another term for Ganapathi Ayyar, used as a sign of respect for the Brahmin landlord and creditor.

Paruthikkaattu Ozhathai Maappillai.description: A Christian oil-mill worker who becomes a successful farmer and leaseholder of Naatrangkaal Naru, later known as Olatheymappillai.

Anthoni of Aatrukkadal.description: A Christian farmer who joins the collective farming effort with Ozhathai Maappillai.

Mathayi of Kol.description: A Christian farmer and businessman, partner in collective farming and later a moneylender.

Thanu Ayyar.description: Ancestral Brahmin cloth merchant from Tamil Nadu who settled in Mangombil and became the founder of a wealthy lineage.

Kittunnik Kaimal.description: Heir to Seerattakaimal, known for transferring property to his wife's family and disregarding traditional customs.

Agavur Nani.description: Wife of Ayyappakuruppu, mistress of Kodanthara, known for her beauty and influence; later becomes Ammaavi.

Nangayyar.description: Elderly woman, mother of Kunjamma, who becomes bedridden and eventually dies.

Kunjamma.description: Nangayyar's youngest daughter, lives in a dream world, mother of Thripurasundari.

Thripurasundari.description: Kunjamma's daughter, seen as the future of the Kodanthara family.

Seelandhippillai Kalyaniyamma.description: Mother of Kesavan, a respected woman who values education and tradition.

Kesavan.description: Son of Kalyaniyamma, a lively and intelligent boy who becomes a teacher and later a clerk.

Mangalacheri Madhupillai.description: Landlord and office-bearer involved in temple disputes and family property conflicts.

Ittiraman Pillai.description: Member of the Konnotthu family, involved in property disputes and lawsuits against Kallaraykkal Raman Pillai.

Kunhammayi.description: Eldest woman of the Konnotthu branch, speaks of the family's hardships.

Kunjunji.description: Individual who travels from Paadi to Paruthikkadu, possibly a family member or messenger.

Kunjachan.description: Relative of Mathayi, successful farmer and businessman in the eastern hills.

Vattathara Peeli.description: Business partner of Mathayi, later becomes a successful independent businessman.

Thoma.description: Peeli's eldest son, wealthy plantation owner and innovator in agricultural labor practices.

Kunjjeli.description: Thoma's wife, who transforms from emaciated to prosperous after marriage.

Paloothra Kunjan.description: Temple farmer devoted to agricultural work, trusted by the Pulayas, dies heartbroken after a betrayal.

Ravippillai.description: Relative of Mangalacheri Madhupillai, whose debts cause family property loss.

Kanakkulathu Pappupillai.description: Honest and upright farmer, respected for his integrity in dealings with Ganapathi Ayyar.

Kunjhan of Uppamparambu.description: One of the 'Trimurthis,' a former ploughman who becomes the temple administrator.

Paman Karthaavu.description: One of the 'Trimurthis,' former overseer for the Konnotthu family, father of Lakshmi.

Ittunnan of Sudhoorathu.description: One of the 'Trimurthis,' known for his sharp tongue and unconventional family life.

Lakshmi.description: Daughter of Kalikkunjhamma and Paraman Karthavu, raised separately after her mother's death.

Kalikkunjhamma.description: Kunjhamma who dies during childbirth, mother of Lakshmi.

Araykattu Kochunani.description: Ittunnan's third wife, with whom he has a harmonious marriage.

Therumathu Kondikkuruppu.description: Oldest man in the village, respected elder who persuades Kunjhan Pillai to take up temple administration.

Kochu Devi.description: Girl in Kesavan's class, whom he likes and wishes to marry.

Kochutti.description: Kochu Devi's elder sister, whose marriage is arranged by Kochunni Nair.

Kochunni Nair.description: Maternal uncle and head of Kochu Devi's family, wields authority over family decisions.

Mathaiyar.description: Mother of Kochu Devi, upholds family honor and refuses Kesavan's marriage proposal.

Suttikkunjamma.description: Kunjamma who becomes pregnant by a Brahmin and is later helped by Kunjangarasaar.

Kunjangarasaar.description: Devasthanam boatman of lower caste who helps Suttikkunjamma.

Peerukannu Mudalali.description: Shopkeeper and landlord, descendant of a Seeratta son-in-law who converted to Islam.

Amina.description: Court official who oversees the eviction of the Seeratta women.

Chennan Pulayan.description: Pulaya bonded laborer with three wives, lives in the purakkalam and later loses his family.

Vattathaan.description: Chennan's son, becomes a fisherman, converts to Islam, and is renamed Pareed.

Sulaiman.description: Landlord and master of Vattathaan (Pareed), arranges his marriage and supports him.

Krishnapillai.description: Current head of the Konnoth family, known for his obsession with chasing flies.

Kunjun Pillai.description: Administrator of the Devasthanam, wishes to retire and hand over responsibilities.

Krishnathirumeny.description: Head of Palathol House, considered for Devasthanam administration.

Moolappadathu Govindan.description: Potential candidate for Devasthanam administration, but his parentage is questioned.

Nattasseri Padmanabhan.description: Wealthy and arrogant man, considered but rejected for Devasthanam administration.

Vettikkattu Nanukkuruppu.description: Respected cook, brings his son-in-law Parameswaran to Kesavapillai for blessings.

Parameswaran.description: Nanukkuruppu's son-in-law, whom he hopes will become a judge.

Konnothu.description: A prominent family or lineage in the village, often holding leadership roles.

Kodanthra.description: Another major family or lineage in the village, associated with temple leadership.

Seeratta.description: A significant family or branch, with its own mansion and leadership.

Kallaraykkal.description: A branch of the Konnothu family, involved in inheritance and property disputes.

Mangombu.description: A village or locality, home to Ganapathi Ayyar and the Swami's math.

Naatrangkaal Naru.description: A tract of forty acres of fertile land, considered among the best in the village.

Aatrukkadal.description: A locality or family name, associated with Anthoni.

Kol.description: A locality or family name, associated with Mathayi.

math.description: A Brahmin religious institution or monastery, often involved in landholding and lending.

Aatrithara.description: A family or locality, associated with marital ties and property transfers.

Ammaavi.description: Title for the respected lady or matriarch of a household.

Kalasip.description: A laborer or worker, sometimes used for those who do odd jobs or manual labor.

Sthani.description: A title for the head of a family or a person holding a hereditary office.

Ettukattu.description: Traditional eight-pillared mansion, typical of Kerala aristocratic families.

Kadammattu.description: A family or locality, associated with Kochikki and property disputes.

Changanassery.description: A town in Kerala, known as a commercial and educational center.

Palai.description: A town in the eastern hills of Kerala, associated with rubber plantations.

Mundampadam.description: A large paddy field in Mangombu, leased by Thoma.

urulai.description: Traditional water-lifting device used in paddy fields.

vadakkayiru.description: Rope mechanism used with the urulai for irrigation.

sahib.description: Term used for a European or white man, often a plantation owner.

Ponmudampuraan.description: Title or nickname for a local ruler or landlord.

Pulaya.description: A Dalit (formerly 'untouchable') caste, traditionally agricultural laborers.

praadu.description: A legal suit or case, especially regarding property or debt.

Pandinadu.description: A region in Tamil Nadu, referenced in caste and migration contexts.

Maravan.description: A Tamil caste, here used as a slur for someone considered untrustworthy.

Paraiyan.description: A Dalit caste in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, traditionally considered 'untouchable.'

Madan.description: A local spirit or deity worshipped by lower castes.

abhisheka pedestal.description: Platform used for ritual bathing of the deity during temple festivals.

yakshi.description: A female spirit or supernatural being in Kerala folklore.

nendran bananas.description: A variety of plantain banana popular in Kerala.

Parayan.description: Another Dalit caste, similar to Pulayar.

Dharmashastras.description: Ancient Hindu legal and ethical texts.

Trimurthis.description: The 'three great ones,' here referring to the trio of village leaders.

Uppamparambu.description: A locality or family name, associated with Kunjhan.

Mukkol.description: A locality or family name, associated with Paman Karthaavu.

Sudhoorathu.description: A locality or family name, associated with Ittunnan.

Vaiparacheri.description: A locality or family, associated with Nani and Kochunnyamma.

Aravathu stone.description: A specific stone or location, possibly a ritual site.

Sthaninayar.description: Title for a Nair holding a hereditary office.

Kodupunna.description: A locality or family, associated with Sthaninayar.

Eriyetra property.description: A property or landholding where a new branch of the family is established.

Kadukkathra.description: A family or locality, associated with Kochunni Nair and Kochudevi.

Seelandhippillai.description: A family name, associated with Kalyaniyamma and Kesavan.

Peerukannu.description: Another name for Beerukannu Mudalali, referencing his lineage.

Moolappadathu.description: A family or household, associated with Govindan.

Sunakkulathu Kittunayar.description: A villager who, along with others, shares in the sorrow over the decline of the temple and village.

Chennattu Kunjunayar.description: A hardworking member of the Chennattu family, known for his resourcefulness and for supporting his extended family; later referred to as Kunjunayar.

Chennattu Kesavan.description: Younger brother of Chennattu Kunjunayar, a celebrated Kathakali performer in the northern regions.

Kunjhan Pillai.description: A member of the Uppamparambu family, involved in the temple administration.

Ganapathi Namboothiri.description: A Brahmin and clever administrator of the temple, whose actions and leadership are both praised and criticized in the village.

Krishnan Namboothiri.description: Elder brother of Ganapathi Namboothiri, who criticizes his brother's handling of temple property.

Kunjunni Kaimal.description: A respected elder of the Soriyan family, honored during the temple festival.

Kunjammai.description: Wife of Ganapathi Namboothiri, originally from the Madampikkal family of Chertala.

Kochudevi.description: A bold buttermilk vendor from the Konoth family who leads a group of women in challenging social norms at the temple festival.

Mathullavan.description: A Christian tenant farmer from Aatrukkadavu who supplies paddy to the Devasthanam.

Sauriyar.description: A Christian tenant farmer from Paruthikkadu who also supplies paddy to the Devasthanam.

Bhavathrathan Namboothiri.description: A Brahmin from the Kangothu family who, after the Mappila riots, is forcibly converted to Islam and becomes Ahmad.

Thothrakkutty Antharjanam.description: Daughter of Bhavathrathan Namboothiri, also converted to Islam and renamed Amina.

Samu Menon.description: Steward of the Kangkothu house, involved in collecting rent and caught up in the Mappila rebellion.

Chinnammu.description: Daughter of Samu Menon, who is abducted and later dies during the Mappila rebellion.

Moidhu.description: A young Muslim who loves Chinnammu and tries to protect her during the rebellion.

Kangkothu Ahmad Kunji.description: Leader of the Mappila group during the rebellion, responsible for capturing and converting Bhavathrathan.

Govindan.description: A member of the Keelmel house, who helps decide how to host Bhavathrathan and his daughter.

Namboothiri Govindan.description: A Brahmin at the Keelmel house who listens to Bhavathrathan's account of the Mappila rebellion.

Kunjumalu Amma.description: Wife of Chennadan, mother to their children, and a central figure in the Athippuraykkal family.

Eechara Pillai.description: Supervisor of the paddy granary, husband of Unnachiyammai, and an honest official who faces hardship.

Unnachiyammai.description: Daughter of Seelanthippillai Paramu Vathiyar, wife of Eechara Pillai, and mother of Kunjumalu.

Madhupillai.description: Eechara Pillai's maternal uncle and former supervisor of the paddy stores, from the Ezham Pillai family.

Seelanthippillai Paramu Vathiyar.description: Father of Unnachiyammai, a respected figure in the village.

Kochittooli.description: Wife of Paramu Vathiyar, mother of Unnachiyammai.

Kunjumalu.description: Wife of Chennadan, mother to their children, and a central figure in the Athippuraykkal family.

Kochchunangi.description: Sister of Kunjunayar, responsible for feeding her large family after her uncle's death.

Kunjhu.description: Nickname for Chennattu Kunjunayar in his youth.

Athippuraykkal Raghavan Pillai.description: Kunjumalu’s younger brother, a teacher who later buys a plantation and is involved in family property disputes.

Kochunangai.description: Sister of Kunjunayar, mother of eight children, and a source of family tension.

Kochukittan.description: Eldest son-in-law in the Chennattu family, involved in property and family disputes.

Madhavan Pillai.description: Eechara Pillai’s eldest son-in-law, who claims inheritance rights to family property.

Elampillil Madhavan Pillai.description: Plaintiff in the court case over Athippuraykkal property, arguing for inheritance through marumakkathayam.

Kunjanna Nair.description: Son of Kunjachi, a teacher, Gandhian, and social reformer who leads many progressive movements in the village.

Kunjachi.description: Mother of Kunjanna Nair, a maid at the Palathol house.

Manikandan.description: Son of Chennadan and Kunjumalu Amma, a bright student and budding poet.

Viswanathan.description: Manikandan’s close friend, son of a school headmistress, and fellow student.

Sarada.description: A girl in Manikandan’s class who cares for him.

Surendran.description: A friend of Manikandan, involved in labor organizing and trade union activities among Pulayars and Parayars.

Ponnamma.description: Surendran’s wife, whom he marries to avoid temptation.

Paachu.description: Ganapathi Namboothiri’s boatman, later found murdered; also a hotel worker who supports his family.

Parayan Idyappan.description: A member of the Parayan caste, first to walk on public roads after untouchability restrictions are lifted.

Vettippurakkal Kunjannayar.description: Teacher who admits Ezhava children to school, follower of Gandhiji and Sree Narayana Guru.

Kochuraman Vaidyar.description: Prominent Ezhava in the village, prefers to maintain caste distinctions.

Nattacheri Padmanabhan.description: A villager who funds legal action against Ganapathi Namboothiri.

Krishnan Pillai.description: Appointed as the new temple manager after the receiver administration.

Vattathara Grigory.description: A prominent Christian who helps organize the Congress conference.

Paruthikkattu Thomas.description: Another leading Christian involved in the Congress conference.

Suren.description: A friend of Manikandan, involved in labor organizing and trade union activities among Pulayars and Parayars.

Karthiyayani.description: Beneficiary of Kunjanna Nair’s will, along with her unborn child.

Puranas.description: Ancient Hindu scriptures containing mythological stories and teachings.

Kali Yuga.description: The current age in Hindu cosmology, often described as an era of decline and moral decay.

Dharma.description: A key concept in Indian religions, meaning righteousness, moral order, or duty.

Palathol.description: A prominent family or house in the village.

Madampikkal.description: A family or lineage, here from Chertala.

Konoth.description: A family or lineage in the village.

Ashtabandha Kalasam.description: A special Hindu ritual for restoring the power of a temple idol.

Aatrukkadavu.description: A place or locality, home to Mathullavan.

Paruthikkadu.description: A place or locality, home to Sauriyar.

Antharjanam.description: A term for Namboothiri Brahmin women.

Kathakali.description: A classical dance-drama from Kerala, known for its elaborate costumes and storytelling.

Mappila.description: A Muslim community in Kerala; also refers to the Mappila rebellion.

Travancore.description: A princely state in southern Kerala.

Shudra.description: The lowest of the four varnas (castes) in traditional Hindu society.

Keelmel.description: A family or house name in the village.

Kangkothu.description: A family or house name, involved in the Mappila rebellion story.

Varyantra.description: A house or estate name in Alappuzha.

Ezhava.description: A prominent caste in Kerala, historically considered lower caste and often associated with social reform.

Vedippurakkal.description: A family or house name, also used as a prefix for Kunjannayar.

Gandhiji.description: Refers to Mahatma Gandhi, leader of the Indian independence movement.

Sree Narayana Guru.description: A revered social reformer and spiritual leader among the Ezhavas and other communities in Kerala.

Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Sangham.description: An organization founded by Sree Narayana Guru to promote social reform and upliftment.

Nair Service Society.description: A community organization for the Nair caste, promoting their welfare and interests.

Ponnuthampuran Thirunal.description: A festival or celebration associated with the Maharaja.

Sri Padmanabhan.description: Refers to Lord Padmanabha, the presiding deity of the Travancore royal family; also used on currency.

Erumelil.description: A place or region, likely referring to Erumeli in Kerala.

Bharat Mata ki Jai.description: A patriotic slogan meaning 'Victory to Mother India'.

Vaikom.description: A town in Kerala, famous for the Vaikom Satyagraha against untouchability.

Satyagraha.description: A form of nonviolent protest popularized by Mahatma Gandhi.

Harijan.description: A term used by Gandhi for people considered 'untouchable' in the caste system.

Balasena.description: A youth group or brigade, here involved in community action.

Puthupparambu.description: A place or house name, bequeathed in Kunjanna Nair’s will.

Kondal.description: A term or name mentioned in the context of prayers for Manikandan.

Paraiyar.description: A Dalit caste, similar to Parayan, found in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

betel.description: A leaf from the betel plant, often chewed with areca nut and lime as a mild stimulant.

plantain leaf.description: A large leaf from the banana plant, traditionally used as a plate for serving food in Kerala.

veshti.description: A traditional South Indian garment, a rectangular cloth worn around the waist.

kanji.description: A rice gruel or porridge, a staple food in Kerala.

ashram.description: A spiritual hermitage or community, often associated with Gandhian or religious movements.

arrack.description: A distilled alcoholic drink made from fermented sap of coconut flowers or sugarcane.

tahsildar.description: A revenue administrative officer in charge of a taluk or sub-district.

sovereign.description: A gold coin, often used as a measure of wealth or dowry.

satyagrahi.description: A participant in satyagraha, or nonviolent resistance.

receiver.description: A court-appointed administrator to manage property or institutions during legal disputes.

bhajans.description: Devotional songs sung in praise of deities, often in group settings.

paddy-threshing room.description: A room used for threshing and processing harvested paddy.

Malancheri Pappi.description: Matriarch of the Malancheri family, whose fortunes rise due to her son's success abroad.

Gopalakrishnan.description: Pappiyamma's son who works in Malaya, sends money home, and later dies in the war; a symbol of migration and sacrifice.

Pappiyamma.description: Mother of Gopalakrishnan, a lender of gold and money in the village, and a central figure in her family's prosperity.

Levadevi.description: A woman who lends gold and gives loans, possibly a moneylender in the community.

Chennattu Kunjannayar.description: A villager who often borrows from Pappiyamma, once her secret lover, and later a symbol of the older generation.

Vattathara Krikary.description: A prominent farmer in the village, involved in land disputes and agricultural politics.

Paruthikkattu Kocheuseppu.description: A large Christian landowner and farmer, representative of the rising Christian agrarian class.

Aathumali Anthoni.description: Another major Christian landowner, illustrating the shift in land ownership.

Srinivasaiyyar.description: A wealthy moneylender and landowner from Mangombu, central to the village's debt issues.

Grigory.description: A farmer and activist working for debt relief, involved in village politics.

Diwanji.description: The chief minister or high official of the princely state, whose birthday celebration becomes a political flashpoint.

Thomas.description: Son of Kochauthayi from Paruthikkadu, a Congress youth opposing the Diwanji's reception.

Philip.description: Son of the Karikari from Vattathara, a Congress youth.

Varghese.description: Son of Anthony from Aathumala, a Congress youth.

Sridharan.description: A youth involved in the Congress opposition to the Diwanji's reception.

Kaurikkunjamma.description: A mother whose sons serve in the army, known for her hospitality to the postman.

Vasudevan.description: Kaurikkunjamma's son, who joins the army and dies in the war.

Krishnan.description: Kaurikkunjamma's younger son, who also joins the army and dies.

Gaurikkutty.description: A woman who tends to the postman with devotion, possibly another name for Kaurikkunjamma.

Seeratta Gopalan.description: A man who becomes wealthy during the war by trading in paddy and rice.

Seeratta Gopalakkaimal.description: Another name for Seeratta Gopalan, emphasizing his status.

Abdul Razak.description: A descendant of Beerukannu, current owner of the Seeratta estate, who returns land to its Hindu owners after independence.

Suleiman.description: Abdul Razak's younger brother, who wishes to migrate to Pakistan after Partition.

Parayathra Paachu.description: A man who becomes wealthy during the war by supplying wooden goods.

Pappa.description: Sotha's daughter, a laborer and activist, involved with Surendran.

Kuttappan.description: Pappa's husband, who complains about her relationship with Surendran.

Neeli.description: Kannan's daughter, rumored to have a child by Surendran.

Gauriyamma.description: A woman arrested during the Quit India movement.

Thamas.description: A man arrested during the Quit India movement.

Gopalan Nayar.description: Neighbor who reads the Bhagavatam to Kunjunayar on his deathbed.

Malancheri.description: A family and house in the village, symbolizing changing fortunes.

Malaya.description: Historical term for present-day Malaysia, where many Malayalis migrated for work.

Math.description: A Hindu monastic institution or religious establishment, often holding land and lending money.

Congress.description: Refers to the Indian National Congress, the main political party leading the independence movement.

INA.description: Indian National Army, a force formed by Indian nationalists in Southeast Asia during WWII to fight for independence.

Bhagavatam.description: A major Hindu scripture, also known as the Bhagavata Purana.

Ekadasha Skandham.description: The eleventh section or canto of the Bhagavatam, considered significant in ritual readings.

Koyirpuram.description: A locality or house plot in the village, site of Kunjunayar and Kunjumalu Amma's funeral.

Makkaal.description: Name of a paddy field or locality in the village.

Seeratta Mana.description: The ancestral home of the Seeratta family.

Vattathara.description: A locality or family name, associated with Krikary and Philip.

Aathumala.description: A locality or family name, associated with Anthoni and Varghese.

Mathakoyil.description: A church or parish in the region.

Mahabali.description: A legendary king in Kerala mythology, associated with the Onam festival.

Thunbeghat.description: A locality or family name, associated with Gauriyar.

Gauriyar.description: A title or name, possibly denoting a community leader or elder.

Parayars.description: A Dalit (formerly 'untouchable') caste traditionally engaged in agricultural labor.

pongal.description: A traditional South Indian rice dish, often eaten during festivals.

Dharma Chakra.description: The 'Wheel of Dharma', a symbol on the Indian national flag.

Mahatmaji.description: A respectful term for Mahatma Gandhi.

pujas.description: Hindu religious rituals or worship ceremonies.

darbha grass.description: A sacred grass used in Hindu rituals and funerals.

Mana.description: A traditional Namboothiri Brahmin ancestral home in Kerala.

Quit India.description: Refers to the Quit India Movement, a mass protest demanding an end to British rule in India.

lathi charge.description: A police tactic involving charging a crowd with long bamboo sticks (lathis) to disperse them.

money order.description: A method of sending money by post, common before widespread banking.

telegram.description: A message sent by telegraph, often used for urgent or official communication.

sharecropping.description: A system where farmers cultivate land owned by others and share the produce.

tricolour.description: The Indian national flag, with three horizontal bands of color.

party.description: Refers to the Communist Party or a similar political organization active in Kerala's labor movement.

Sadanandan.description: The Left (Communist) candidate, known for his role in the Punnapra Vayalar struggle.

Paruthikkattu Kochousepp.description: A landlord who, along with Krikary, attempts to control workers and elections.

Vattathra Philipose.description: A wealthy candidate opposing Surendran in the panchayat elections, willing to buy votes.

Pamupillai.description: A member of the Seelanthippillil family, now working in Kochi, who supports his sister Gauriyamma.

Paramupillai.description: A family member of Seelanthippillil who remains unmarried and helps Gauri.

Arya Antharjanam.description: Vasudevan's wife, living with him and their children in the Palathol house.

Subhadra.description: Daughter of Vasudevan and Arya Antharjanam.

Valiyakunjathi.description: Son of the elder Pulayan, who boldly addresses Krikari, symbolizing changing social relations.

Karuthai.description: A laborer whose corpse is found floating in the river, representing the violence of the era.

Koya.description: Watchman at the choultry in Thiruvananthapuram who shelters Manikandan.

Saleel.description: Surendran's son by Pappa, a union secretary and adversary to Surendran in the factory strike.

Kadukkathra Kunjukuttan.description: A former Naxalite who applies for a job at the factory, struggling with his past.

Anthoni of Aatrukkadavu.description: An elderly landlord, part of the trio reflecting on the changes in the village.

Kochouseph of Paruthikkadu.description: An elderly landlord, part of the trio reflecting on the changes in the village.

Poovachaal Paili.description: A man who temporarily holds Krikari's land as a benami during the land ceiling.

Suppaiyan.description: The first to bring the term 'Saar' (Sir) to the village, remembered for his romance with Seelanthippillil Kalyaniyamma.

Nattacheriy Ramachandran Pillai.description: Father of Madhu and Nalini, struggling to secure his children's futures.

Madhu.description: Son of Ramachandran Pillai, who elopes with Rosakkutty.

Nalini.description: Madhu's younger sister, a B.A. graduate awaiting marriage.

Rosakkutty.description: A college student from the Aatrukkadalil family who elopes with Madhu.

Damodaran.description: Gopalakkaimal's educated son, who does not help with family work.

Narayana Panicker.description: Panchayat member who learns about the Land Tribunal and its implications.

Paruthikkattu Kochouthayam.description: A landlord who, along with others, fears the coming land reform.

Vattathara Karikari.description: A landlord, possibly another spelling of Krikary/Krikori, who fears land reform.

Chain Measurer Nagam Pillai.description: A figure from the past known for measuring land boundaries.

Konnothu Vallyachan.description: Ancestral figure, once a village leader, now referenced as a ghostly presence.

Paruthikkattu Olatha.description: A figure from the past, referenced as a ghostly presence.

Thunbekkalavan.description: A landlord terrified by the Naxalite threat.

Murugan.description: A laborer killed by Philip in the Thodarchi hills.

Paruthikkattu Sochchoth.description: A villager who asks the crucial question about food security at the end of the chapter.

Begkal fields.description: A locality or group of fields in the village, associated with Gauriyar.

Communist.description: Refers to the Communist Party and its ideology, influential in Kerala's politics and land reforms.

Punnapra Vayalar.description: Refers to the Punnapra-Vayalar uprising, a historic Communist-led workers' revolt in Kerala in 1946.

Vayalar.description: A village in Kerala, site of the famous Punnapra-Vayalar uprising.

Aatrukkadalil.description: A Christian family in the village, home of Rosakkutty.

Sirattai.description: A locality in the village where Kunjamma, the orphaned woman, lived.

Kazhimukham.description: A beach in Thiruvananthapuram where Manikandan wanders and a suicide occurs.

Kuttanad.description: A region in Kerala known for its vast paddy fields and backwaters.

Balathol house.description: A family house in the village, associated with Vasudevan.

Pulayan.description: A Dalit caste traditionally associated with agricultural labor in Kerala.

Parayas.description: A Dalit caste in Kerala, traditionally agricultural laborers.

Naxalite.description: A member of the radical Communist movement in India, inspired by the Naxalbari uprising.

Kadukathra Kunnukkutty.description: A village or locality associated with Naxalite activity.

Devaswom.description: A temple trust or administrative body managing Hindu temples in Kerala.

Kalasiper.description: Likely a local deity or temple figure, mentioned in connection with donations.

Erumathra Madam.description: A religious or community building donated to the Kalasiper.

Land Tribunal.description: A government office established to implement land reform laws and settle land disputes.

Panchayat.description: The local self-government body at the village level in India.

Panchayat hall.description: The building where the panchayat meets.

Land Reform Act.description: A law passed to redistribute land from landlords to tenants and the landless.

Pattas.description: Legal documents granting ownership or tenancy rights to land.

Thodarchi hills.description: A hilly region or estate area in the east, associated with Philip and laborers.

Mangalassery.description: A locality with karisal lands that have been converted to house plots.

Seelanthippillil.description: A family or house in the village, associated with Kalyaniyamma and others.

Saar.description: A Malayalam adaptation of 'Sir', used as a respectful address for superiors.

Karthika wind.description: A seasonal wind in Kerala, associated with the Karthika star and agricultural cycles.

Kaalaar river.description: A river in the region, source of floods and irrigation.

Gandharvans.description: Mythical celestial beings in Hindu tradition, believed to inhabit family homes.

Panchayat President Tenant Surendran.description: Refers to Surendran's dual role as both panchayat president and tenant leader.

Kochoutha.description: A landlord, possibly another spelling of Kochouthayam.

Palathol family.description: A once-prominent family in the village, now impoverished.

Suppaiyan Saar.description: Suppaiyan, who introduced the term 'Saar' to the village.

sickle.description: A curved, hand-held agricultural tool used for harvesting crops.

constituency.description: A geographic area represented by an elected official.

open votes.description: Votes cast openly, often under the supervision or pressure of landlords, as opposed to secret ballots.

registers.description: Official records, often referring to land or tenancy records.

pamphlet.description: A small booklet or leaflet containing information or political propaganda.

pit notice.description: A public notice, often posted in a conspicuous place, used for accusations or announcements.

panchayat.description: The local self-government council at the village level in India.

ward.description: A division or district within a panchayat or municipality, represented by an elected member.

tharavadu.description: The ancestral joint family home and system in Kerala.

kuthuvilakku.description: A traditional South Indian oil lamp, used in rituals and ceremonies.

patta.description: A legal document granting ownership or tenancy rights to land.

lessor.description: A person who leases land or property to another.

tenant.description: A person who occupies land or property rented from a landlord.

landlord.description: A person who owns and leases land to tenants.

archana.description: A Hindu ritual involving the chanting of names and offering of flowers or rice to a deity.

pooja.description: A Hindu act of worship or ritual.

benami.description: A property held in the name of another person to conceal the real owner's identity.

coolie.description: A manual laborer, especially one employed in agriculture or construction.

palmyra.description: A type of palm tree, whose leaves are used for thatching and writing manuscripts.

naal.description: A traditional unit of land area in Kerala.

Inquilab Zindabad.description: A revolutionary slogan in Urdu/Hindi meaning 'Long live the revolution'.

land ceiling.description: A legal limit on the amount of land one family or individual can own.

pattas.description: Legal documents granting ownership or tenancy rights to land.

class enemy.description: A person or group seen as an adversary of the working class, especially in Communist ideology.

gruel.description: A thin porridge made by boiling rice or other grains in water, often eaten by the poor.

seedling land.description: Land used for growing young rice plants before transplanting.
